implementation_notes: Swift has no message header to fill in, so the return address is a value in the request: a @Sendable reply closure, or a CheckedContinuation captured by an actor when bridging a callback-based client into async/await — invoking the closure or resuming the continuation is the reply. Sendable checking is what makes this safe across actor boundaries. On a real broker (MQTT 5 Response Topic, AMQP reply-to) the address is a header again, so keep the continuation shape for in-process services and the property for wire messages.
idiom_name: reply closure / withCheckedContinuation carried in the request
pitfalls: withCheckedContinuation must be resumed exactly once on every path including errors — the checked form traps at runtime when it is not, the unsafe form corrupts state silently.
@Sendable reply closures capture the requester's state into whatever context invokes them, so resuming from another executor requires the capture to be safe or actor isolation to be re-entered.
A reply closure stored beyond the request's lifetime retains the caller's objects and can leak a view controller or session; capture weakly or give continuations an explicit timeout.
